before: In this DOM example a click starts on the inner span and bubbles through its ancestors. event.target is the originating element; event.currentTarget is the element whose listener is currently running. A listener on the containing div can handle child controls without registering a separate listener on each one.

target.closest("button[data-topic]") returns the nearest matching element, including target itself, or null. root.contains(button) checks that the result is still within the delegated area. dataset.topic reads the data-topic attribute. Inputs here are click events from Elements in the supplied markup, not arbitrary non-Element event targets.

installDelegation returns dispose, a no-argument function that detaches the listener. With bubbles:false the ancestor listener does not receive this child event. Optional practice: dispatch on the non-action paragraph and explain why nothing is recorded. Actual local evidence may use JSDOM with the production frame harness; that is not a real-browser interaction or rendering test.
after:
A click can travel from the clicked element up through its parent elements. This is called bubbling.

We can put one click listener on a group of buttons. It can handle clicks from inside the group. This is called event delegation.

`event.target` is where the click started. `event.currentTarget` is where the listener is running.

`target.closest("button[data-topic]")` looks for the nearest button with a `data-topic` attribute. It checks the target itself, then its parents. It returns `null` if it finds none.

`root.contains(button)` checks that the button is inside our group. `button.dataset.topic` reads its `data-topic` text. In this example, the click starts on an HTML element.

`installDelegation` returns a cleanup function. We name it `dispose`. Calling it removes the listener, using the same `onClick` function that was added.

Complete the guard in the starter. A click on the paragraph must add nothing to the log. After cleanup, clicks must also add nothing.

The example sends a test event through the page. It does not test how a person clicks or uses a keyboard.

before.question: If the synthetic child click has bubbles:false, does the div listener record it?
choices: Yes. currentTarget always becomes the child.
No. This child event does not bubble to the ancestor listener.
Yes. Every synthetic event must bubble regardless of its option.
before.explanation: The listener is registered on the ancestor for the bubbling phase; this event never reaches that listener by bubbling.

after.question: Will the group listener receive this child click if bubbles is false?
choices: Yes. currentTarget always becomes the child.
No. The click does not bubble up to this listener.
after.explanation: This listener waits for clicks that bubble up to the group. With bubbles set to false, the child click does not reach it.
